HW7 · A gradient step, a fit, and a digit’s DCT

Out Thursday November 19 · due Wednesday November 25 (the holiday stays free), 11:59 PM on Canvas · 2.5 % of the course grade · JavaScript or Python · hub · schedule · syllabus · all homework
Read before this homework: Neural Networks and Embeddings §1 and §2 · §3, backpropagation · The Space of Images §4, the Fourier basis · §8, what JPEG keeps · §9, PSNR

What you build

Small on purpose: six days, and nothing out over Thanksgiving. First the text's tiny network by hand: one forward pass, one backward pass, one step. Then the same code trains the 12-unit network on the course's 12 wave samples. Then a digit through the discrete cosine transform: keep the lowest k × k frequencies, rebuild, and measure what was lost in decibels.

JavaScriptPythonWhat it computes
forwardforwardah = tanh(w1h x + b1h), f = b2 + Σ w2h ah.
gradientsgradientsThe mean squared error over the samples and its gradient with respect to w1, b1, w2, b2, by backpropagation.
sgdStepsgd_stepA new model, each parameter moved by −lr times its gradient.
dct2dct2The orthonormal 2D DCT-II of an n × n image.
idct2Truncatedidct2_truncatedThe image rebuilt from the k × k low-frequency block only.
psnrpsnr10 log10(1 / MSE) for pixel values in [0, 1].
  • The tiny net: w1 = (1, −1), b1 = (0.5, 0.5), w2 = (0.8, −0.6), b2 = 0.1, one sample x = 0.4, y = 0.3, lr = 0.1.
  • The fit starts from the seeded 12-unit weights and 12 samples in data.json (the JavaScript track imports the same values from lib/skeletons/data-hw07.js).
  • The digit is the first 3 of the course's 2,000 digits, 20 × 20, gray in [0, 1], row-major.

Implement and replace

Build each function from primitives (arithmetic, tanh, cos, log10; in Python, NumPy arrays and products.) and use the engine's own helper, where one exists, only to check your result. These are off limits in your submission:

TrackOff limits
WebGL (JavaScript)Any machine-learning or signal-processing library. Plain arrays and loops.
Pythonscipy, torch, jax and any autodiff; np.fft and any DCT routine. NumPy arrays, dot and matrix products are allowed.

Getting started

WebGL track.
  1. Download the course site: its repository (Code, then Download ZIP), or git clone it.
  2. From the site's root folder run python3 -m http.server 8000 and open http://localhost:8000/homework/run.html?hw=hw07.
  3. Edit lib/skeletons/hw07.js, the only file you change, and reload: the Checks table under the scene compares your numbers with the ones below.

The unfilled skeleton runs on this site too, so you can see the page before you start.

Python track.
  1. From the same download, open homework/hw07/hw07.ipynb in Jupyter or VS Code, with data.json and expected.json in the same folder.
  2. Fill in the functions marked TODO and run all cells: the last cell prints each check with your value and the expected one.

Submitting and grading

  • WebGL: the one file hw07.js.
  • Python: the notebook hw07.ipynb, run, with the check cell's output visible.

Grading runs your functions twice: on the published inputs above and on a second set of inputs that is not published. A check earns its points only when your value is within its tolerance on both, so the numbers have to come from the math. The score is the sum of the points earned, out of 100. A submission that does not load or compile earns no check points. Name any collaborators and tools in the submission comment.

Late tokens. You have two for the quarter. Declare one in the submission comment to extend this homework by 24 hours without penalty. Beyond tokens, late homework loses 10 % per day for up to three days.
